Nora: FYI just watched a new hire get blocked on the python sample: API returned 401 with JSON {\"message\":\"api key expired\",\"code\":\"auth.expired\"} but the app displayed 'Request failed' and no action. Oof.
Diego: That's the transport rewrap bug we've seen. py was converting some 4xx into a generic TransportError when retries were enabled.
Hannah: Node/Go surfaces AuthError(status=401, code='auth.expired'), with a small metadata map. We should make py match that.
Evan: Minimal cross-sdk contract idea: exception classes: AuthError, RateLimitError, QuotaError, ClientError, ServerError, NetworkError. Each exception MUST include flat metadata keys: status (int), code (string), retryable (bool), retry_after (string|null), hint (string|null).
Nora: +1. For onboarding UX the 'hint' is the most important - short imperative text like 'Run `ri login` to refresh your key.' Sample-app should show that and a one-click CTA if available.
Diego: Implementation notes: map at the HTTP transport boundary and attach parsed body.code if present. Parse Retry-After header to retry_after (support secs or HTTP-date). Don't rewrite 4xx -> 5xx.
Hannah: Also please ensure exception.__str__ is friendly by default. Raw response bodies only when RI_SDK_DEBUG=true. No leaking JSON blobs into the UI.
Evan: Telemetry: tag errors with error_class and error_code so we can detect onboarding spikes (e.g., >10 auth.expired per hour). We'll hook alerts.
Nora: Quick pseudo mapping I sketched:
```\n# transport layer (pseudo)\nif status == 401:\n    raise AuthError(message or body.get('message'), status=status, code=body.get('code'))\nelif status == 429:\n    raise RateLimitError(body.get('message'), status=status, retry_after=headers.get('Retry-After'), code=body.get('code'))\nelif 400 <= status < 500:\n    raise ClientError(body.get('message'), status=status, code=body.get('code'))\nelif status >= 500:\n    raise ServerError('server error', status=status, retryable=True)\n```\nDiego: Tests: add small parity suite asserting that for a given status+body the SDK raises the expected class and that metadata keys exist (status, code, retryable, retry_after, hint). I'll wire this into CI.
Hannah: I'll update sample-app to consume exception.metadata.hint and render CTA (and countdown if retry_after present). Also will replace raw error dump with friendly copy.
Nora: Can someone own the py patch? Seems like low-risk but high-impact for onboarding.
Diego: I'll take it. Plan: add exceptions module, map statuses, include headers/body in metadata (flat), update sample-app, and open PR by EOD.
error-bot: (automated) created ticket INF-5123: \"PY-SDK: avoid opaque transport rewraps; unify exception metadata\" assigned to diego.
Nora: Thanks! Once PR is up drop link here and we'll run a staging canary through the onboarding flow.
Evan: One more: add a short doc snippet showing best practice for callers: switch on exception type first, then fallback to code string. Example in docs.
Diego: Will do. Draft PR: https://git.internal/redwood/py-sdk/pull/271 (draft) — feedback appreciated. :thumbsup:
Nora: Reviewing now. If green, we'll ship a staged canary ASAP.
